subject: Operator action ledger: export mechanics and sampling proposal for compliance pack
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@medicosys.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: audit-team@medicosys.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: operator action ledger export for SOC 2 / SIG evidence

Kimberly —

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG and SOC 2 evidence collection we need a scoped export of "operator action" events from Redwood for the period 2028-07-01 -> 2029-06-30. Our auditor has asked for:

- A tabular extract (CSV or Parquet) listing each operator/event with timestamps, actor id, actor role, action type, target resource (resource id + type), request id/correlation id, IP (if available), and a hash/checksum for integrity.
- A description of what event types are captured by Redwood under "admin/operator actions" (e.g., API key creation, role changes, model pin/rollout, manual cache flushes, emergency fallbacks).
- Retention window and whether on-demand exports will include trimmed/ephemeral events (KV cache evictions, ephemeral session tokens).
- Redaction options for PII (email addresses in actor name fields) and sampling approach if a full-year export is impractical.
- Delivery options (SFTP with signed manifest, presigned S3, or Drive link) and approximate ETA once we approve the scope.

We can provide a minimal CSV schema if that helps — attaching our auditor's template.

Appreciate a clear runbook we can attach to our SIG response.

Best,
Lisa Chen
Security Manager | MedicoSys

Attachment: medicosys_auditor_template.csv (stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@medicosys.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, audit-team@medicosys.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operator action ledger export for SOC 2 / SIG evidence

Hi Lisa —

Thanks for the clear ask and the template. We can produce an operator-action ledger export that meets auditor expectations; below is our proposed scope and options. I kept the wording intentionally explicit so you can paste it into your SIG response if needed.

High-level options (pick one):
1) Full-year canonical export (recommended for completeness): compressed Parquet files partitioned by month, containing all operator events and system metadata. Includes SHA256 manifest + per-file checksum.
2) Sampled export + attest: produce a deterministic stratified sample (by month and action type) plus a hashed-count reconciliation file for the full set, and provide a short explanation of sampling algorithm. Good when customers prefer smaller deliveries.
3) Snapshot + on-demand slices: provide a timeboxed snapshot and run ad-hoc queries for specific auditor questions (e.g., all role-change events).

Fields we can include (default Parquet/CSV columns): event_timestamp_utc, event_type, actor_id (redacted option below), actor_role, actor_email (redaction optional), target_resource_type, target_resource_id, request_id, correlation_id, src_ip, user_agent, outcome (success/fail), raw_payload_summary, event_sequence_id, file_checksum

Retention & coverage: operator events are retained in our operational store for 24 months (rolling). Ephemeral telemetry (short-lived session tokens) is not included by default in the operator-action ledger because it is instrumented in a separate trace store; we can include related artifacts on request but will need to scope.

PII redaction options:
- None (full fields)
- Pseudonymize actor_email (sha256+salt)
- Remove actor_email, keep actor_id and actor_role

Delivery & integrity:
- Preferred: SFTP drop with a signed manifest (SHA256 per file + signed manifest).
- Alternate: presigned s3 + signed manifest or Google Drive link + manifest.
- We provide a chain-of-custody note and an HMAC-signed manifest for auditor verification.

Timing: for a full-year Parquet export we typically need 5 business days after scope sign-off; sampled exports can be done in 48 hours.

Next steps I propose: 1) confirm preferred option (full vs sampled), 2) confirm PII redaction choice, 3) decide delivery method. I also attached a draft export spec CSV you can use as a starting point.

I'll loop in Soojin for the extraction mechanics and checksums.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_export_spec_v1.csv (stub)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@medicosys.com>
Cc: audit-team@medicosys.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2029 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator action ledger export for SOC 2 / SIG evidence

Hi all —

Technical notes on what we can and cannot include in the ledger, so expectations are aligned:

What we log as operator/admin actions (examples):
- api_key.create, api_key.rotate, api_key.revoke
- user.role.update, user.invite, user.disable
- model.pin, model.unpin, model.deploy, model.rollback, model.version.promote
- dedicated.capacity.allocate, dedicated.capacity.deallocate
- policy.change, route.override, fallback.trigger
- manual.kv_cache.invalidate, manual.prefix_cache.flush

For each event we persist: monotonic event_sequence_id, event_timestamp_utc (RFC3339), actor_id (internal UUID), actor_role, actor_email (when available), request_id (trace id), correlation_id, target_resource_type, target_resource_id, event_payload_summary (JSON-safe string), outcome, src_ip (if present), agent_string (if present).

Export mechanics:
- Exports are generated from our operational audit ledger. For full exports we stream monthly partitions to a staging S3 bucket, convert to Parquet with canonical column types, and then compute per-file SHA256. We also generate a manifest.jsonl.gz that includes file paths, row counts, and checksums.
- For sampled exports we use a deterministic hash-based sampler on request_id to ensure reproducible sampling; we also emit reconciliation counts for each month+event_type bucket.

Redaction: PII redaction (actor_email) is performed during export via a stateless pseudonymization function (HMAC-SHA256 with customer-specific salt) or full redaction (empty string) depending on your choice. Note: pseudonymization preserves uniqueness while protecting the cleartext for auditor verification.

Timezone fidelity: we canonicalize all timestamps to UTC in exports and include original timezone metadata when available.

Special cases/ephemeral data: ephemeral session tokens and in-memory ephemeral cache evictions are not part of the canonical ledger unless explicitly instrumented; if you need those, we can include supplemental logs but they will increase extraction time and size.

Operational security: the exported artifacts can be encrypted at rest (S3 SSE-KMS) and we will sign the manifest with our service key. Transfer instructions can include customer KMS key wrapping if required.

Happy to run a short demo of a one-month slice so you can validate schema and redaction choices before the full export.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Infrastructure Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@medicosys.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, audit-team@medicosys.com
Date: Thu, 4 Jul 2029 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator action ledger export for SOC 2 / SIG evidence

Kimberly / Soojin —

Thanks, that level of detail is great. A couple clarifications from the auditor:

1) We will take the full-year canonical export (Parquet) — but please apply pseudonymization to actor_email (HMAC-SHA256 with salt) rather than full redaction. Auditor wants uniqueness preserved.
2) Delivery: SFTP with signed manifest is preferred. We will provide drop credentials shortly.
3) Please include the hashed reconciliation file (monthly counts per event_type) so the auditor can sanity-check sampling if needed.
4) ETA: we need the export delivered by 2029-07-12 to meet audit timelines. If full export cannot be completed by that date, please run the demo one-month slice first (we'll accept that as interim evidence) and then the full export as soon as possible.

Also: can you include a brief statement in the runbook on the retention policy and the mechanism for preserving integrity (checksums + manifest signing)?

Best,
Lisa

On a separate note, audit-team@medicosys.com will follow up with SFTP credentials in the next email.

Lisa —

Acknowledged. Summary of agreed scope and next steps (you can paste to your auditor):

- Scope: Full-year canonical export for 2028-07-01 -> 2029-06-30, format: Parquet, partitioned by month.
- Columns: (as listed previously) with actor_email pseudonymized via HMAC-SHA256 + customer salt.
- Integrity: Per-file SHA256 checksums and signed manifest (HMAC using Redwood service key). We will include monthly reconciliation file (event_type row counts + total rows).
- Delivery: SFTP drop (we'll wait for credentials). Files will be encrypted at rest and transmitted via SFTP.
- ETA: We will deliver a one-month demo slice within 48 hours of receiving SFTP creds; full export target 2029-07-12. If any extraction exception occurs we will notify you immediately and provide interim counts.

Action items assigned:
- MedicoSys: send SFTP credentials and confirm salt for HMAC pseudonymization.
- Redwood (Soojin): prepare demo one-month slice and manifest.
- Redwood (Kimberly): prepare runbook blurb and attach export spec (redwood_export_spec_v1.csv).

I'll send the runbook blurb and a sample manifest within the hour.

Thanks,
Kimberly
